name: Flourish
intro: This is where I cook properly. Whole foods, and a bit more prep.

fl-eggs.label: The eggs
fl-eggs.moment: From the farm up the road. The hens are laying well this week.
moments: Brown eggs, mostly. The hens don't take requests.
I keep them out of the fridge. Hard to say why.

fl-greens.label: The greens
fl-greens.moment: Kale and parsley, picked twenty minutes ago.

fl-range.label: The range
fl-range.moment: I light it first thing and it stays lit all day. The big pan lives on it.

fl-food-processor.label: The food processor
fl-food-processor.moment: Pesto, hummus, a quick pastry crumb. It saves my knuckles a lot of chopping.
moments: Mind the blade when you wash it. I say that to everyone.
It's louder than it looks.

fl-air-fryer.label: The air fryer
fl-air-fryer.moment: Crisp potatoes in twenty minutes. I was suspicious at first. I've come round.
moments: Shake the basket halfway. It likes to be reminded.
It does a very good job of leftovers.

fl-slow-cooker.label: The slow cooker
fl-slow-cooker.moment: Put it on in the morning and supper mostly takes care of itself.
moments: Don't lift the lid to check. It sulks.
Beans, stews, a big pot of something. It's patient, which I'm not.

fl-bbq.label: The barbecue
fl-bbq.moment: For the days the weather behaves. The lid's hot, so mind your hands.
moments: It sits out by the garden door, waiting for a fine evening.
Corn in its husks, whole fish, sausages. I'm easily pleased.

fl-knife-block.label: The knife block
fl-knife-block.moment: Five knives and I use two. A sharp one is easier to control than a dull one.
moments: Slide them in with the edge down, and keep your fingers behind the blade.
Wash and dry them by hand. They'll stay sharper.

fl-scales.label: The scales
fl-scales.moment: For bread and pastry, weighing beats scooping. Cups are for easy days.
moments: Zero the bowl first. I forget about half the time.
Grams don't care how tightly you pack the flour.

fl-colander.label: The colander
fl-colander.moment: Pasta, rinsed beans, washed greens. It's the hardest-working thing on the wall.
moments: It hangs on a hook so it can dry properly.
Rinse tinned beans in it and the sauce turns out cleaner.

fl-skillet.label: The skillet
fl-skillet.moment: Heavy, and it holds its heat. I use it for most things.
moments: Dry it on the stove, then rub in a little oil. Never the dishwasher.
Let it get properly hot before the food goes in.

fl-dresser.label: The kitchen hutch
fl-dresser.moment: Lentils, chickpeas, oats and seeds. Keep these jars full and there's always a good meal.
moments: Everything is labelled. Mostly correctly.
I top the jars up on the first of the month.

fl-trug.label: The trug
fl-trug.moment: Straight out of the beds. Knock the soil off, but don't wash them until you need them.

fl-herbs.label: The herbs
fl-herbs.ref: the herbs on the window ledge
fl-herbs.moment: Rosemary, thyme and mint. They like the sun on this ledge.

fl-phonograph.label: The phonograph
fl-phonograph.moment: Wind the handle and it plays: Grieg, Vivaldi or Dvořák, depending on the hour.
moments: The records came with the house. I've never bought one, and never wanted to.
It skips on the third track. I've stopped minding.
fl-phonograph.moment_stop: Needle up. That'll do for now.
fl-phonograph.moment_quiet: Give the handle a few turns. Turn the sound on, by the bell, and you'll hear it.

fl-window.label: The sea
fl-window.moment: The same bay you see from Cuddlecore, from the other side of the Inn.
moments: The bay looks different from this side. Same water, though.
I wash this window more than the others. Don't ask me why.

Strain, let it cool, and keep it in the fridge for 4 days or the freezer for 3 months.

steps: Wash the herbs and dry them well.
Chop them with the salt until the mix is bright green and fine.
Spread it on a plate for an hour to dry a little.
Keep it in a jar in the fridge and use a pinch on eggs, rice or anything plain.

steps: Put the damp cloth under the board so it doesn't slide.
Curl the fingertips of your holding hand under, like a claw.
Let the flat of the blade rest against your knuckles as you cut.
Cut slowly. Speed comes later.

seed.name: Chilli garlic noodles with a fried egg

seed.name: Quick shakshuka

atoms.freezer: Freezes for up to 3 months, flat in bags. Thaw overnight and reheat until steaming.

atoms.freezer: Freezes for up to 3 months. Leave a gap at the top, thaw overnight and heat until steaming.

atoms.freezer: Freezes for up to 3 months, wrapped. Reheat until steaming hot throughout.

steps: Turn the handle in, over the stove, not out over the room.
Lift a hot pan with a dry cloth, never a damp one, and keep your wrist straight.
Add food to a hot pan away from you, so any splash goes the other way.

atoms.title: Hold a pan safely
atoms.hook: Handle turned in, a dry cloth to hand, and a steady wrist.
atoms.method_short: Keep the handle turned in, over the stove rather than out over the room. Lift with a dry cloth, never a damp one, and a straight wrist. Add food to a hot pan away from you.

steps: Fill the sink with hot soapy water before you start cooking.

Wipe the bench as you go.
Dry up and put things away last.

atoms.title: The ten-minute tidy
atoms.hook: Wash as you go and the clear-up takes ten minutes.

steps: Put the colander in the sink before you lift the pot.
Scoop out a mug of the pasta water and set it aside.
Lift the pot with both hands and tip it away from you, keeping your face back from the steam.
Put the pasta back in the pot and add a splash of the saved water to your sauce.

atoms.title: Drain pasta without scalding yourself
atoms.hook: Colander in the sink first, then tip the pot away from you.

atoms.title: Wholemeal Irish soda bread
atoms.hook: A dense brown loaf with no yeast and no waiting.
atoms.method_short: Mix the flours, baking soda and salt, then stir in buttermilk to a shaggy dough. Shape into a round, cut a cross in the top and bake at 200°C for about 40 minutes, until it sounds hollow when tapped underneath.

seed.name: Wholemeal Irish soda bread
seed.why: A loaf you can make before the butter has softened.

atoms.title: Spanish tortilla with potato and onion
atoms.hook: Potato and onion slow-cooked in oil, set in eggs.
atoms.method_short: Cook thinly sliced potato and onion gently in olive oil until soft, then stir into beaten eggs. Cook in the pan until the base is set, flip with a plate, and cook until no raw egg is left in the middle.

seed.name: Spanish tortilla with potato and onion

atoms.title: Gazpacho, cold and blended
atoms.hook: Ripe tomato, cucumber and pepper, blended and chilled.
atoms.method_short: Blend the tomato, cucumber, pepper and a small clove of garlic until smooth. Add olive oil, a splash of vinegar and salt, and chill for at least an hour before serving cold.

seed.name: Gazpacho, cold and blended
seed.why: Best with tomatoes that taste of something.

atoms.title: Vietnamese summer rolls with prawns
atoms.hook: Rice paper wrapped round noodles, herbs and prawns.
atoms.method_short: Soak the vermicelli, then dip a sheet of rice paper in warm water until pliable. Lay lettuce, herbs, noodles and cooked prawns along the middle, fold in the sides and roll tight. Serve with lime and a dipping sauce.

atoms.title: Gado-gado: Indonesian vegetables with peanut sauce
atoms.hook: Blanched vegetables, egg and tofu under a warm peanut sauce.
atoms.method_short: Boil or steam the potato, beans and cabbage until just tender, and hard-boil the eggs. Warm peanut butter with water, lime and soy sauce into a pourable sauce. Arrange everything on a plate with the tofu and spoon the sauce over.
